title: Adaptive tail-probing calibration and non-linear layer rebalancer for LLama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: When applying mixed-precision (FP8 + INT8 fallback) quantization profiles we observe occasional quality regressions driven by rare per-head activation spikes and cross-layer residual accumulation. These regressions are model-specific — LLama shows high-kurtosis spikes in mid layers, Mistral has distributed light tails across many heads, and Qwen displays occasional attention head bursts on long sequences. Goal: Implement a calibration workflow and runtime-safe transform that (1) detects tail/spike behavior at calibration time, (2) synthesizes conservative per-head scaling transforms for quantization, and (3) applies a lightweight non-linear layer rebalancer at compile/serve time to prevent cumulative bias without unduly increasing activation ranges.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Calibration harness produces per-layer+per-head tail statistics and writes a stable quant-profile artifact for FP8 and INT8 variants. 2) For LLama/Mistral/Qwen baseline eval suites, median token-level logit-distance vs FP32 must be <= 0.015 and top-1 generation divergence <= 0.8% on the regen test set. 3) Runtime rebalancer must not increase 99th-percentile latency by >5ms for p95 requests on dedicated pool. 4) Canary rollout shows no customer-impacting regressions across three internal tenants.
tasks: Design calibration job that probes tail mass: per-head kurtosis, 99.9th percentile, and Weibull tail fit
Implement synthetic tail-probing sampler that augments natural prompts with rare-token/long-context stimuli
Extend existing calib harness to output per-head affine-normalizer parameters and confidence scores
Implement non-linear layer rebalancer kernel (GELU-aware affine adjustment + residual clipping schedule) in runtime-1.22 branch
Add model-specific thresholds for LLama, Mistral, Qwen and unit tests to ensure deterministic calibration outputs
Integrate profile artifact into model registry and runtime fallback mapper (FP8 primary, INT8 fallback with head suppression)
Create evaluation job that runs full regen+semantic tests and logs metrics to perf dashboard
Prepare canary plan and rollout automation (canary traffic, auto-rollback triggers)

notes: Decision: prefer per-head affine-normalizer with confidence-driven masking versus blunt percentile clipping — retains dynamic range for common tokens.
Trade-off: slight added calibration time (approx +15%) to compute Weibull tail fits and synthetic probes, but reduces downstream fallback frequency by estimated 40% on warm models.
Follow-ups: add a telemetry tag to report 'head-suppression-applied' at token-level for 2 weeks during canary to validate reduced regressions.
